subject: Regional warmup + canary fallback — request to validate availability window and credit eligibility
messages:
From: Elena Morales <elena@blueharborpay.com>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.com
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 08:12:00 -0800
Subject: Spike of 503s this morning — please confirm downtime window and credit eligibility

Hi Jonas,

We saw a spike of 503s and end-to-end latency increase on our payment-checkout route this morning between roughly 08:05 and 08:40 PST. Our ops dashboard shows ~6–9% errors during that interval and several failed transactions (trace ids attached). This impacted our BlackCart checkout flow for ~35 minutes and caused a small revenue impact.

Two questions: can Redwood confirm the precise availability/downtime window for our tenant, and does the contract allow for proportional credits if this is deemed an availability breach? We also noticed the routing shifted to a canary fallback node during that time — could you confirm whether those fallback events are included in SLA calculations?

I’m attaching a couple of sample trace ids and a small trace snippet. We’ll need an expedited postmortem and an estimate for any credits so I can brief FIN & Ops. Our contract id is BH-ACCT-99321.

Thanks,
Elena
Elena Morales
Head of Payments | BlueHarbor Payments
attachments: sample_traces.txt (text), checkout_failures.csv (csv)
From: jonas.weber@redwood.com
To: Elena Morales <elena@blueharborpay.com>
Cc: david.kim@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 08:28:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Spike of 503s this morning — please confirm downtime window and credit eligibility

Hi Elena — thanks for the report and the sample traces. Sorry for the disruption. I’ve looped in David (SRE) to start an immediate telemetry pull and Laura (your AM) to keep your stakeholders updated.

Next steps from our side:
- David will pull the raw traces and routing logs for 07:50–09:00 PST and provide a preliminary window.
- We’ll check whether the canary fallback you saw was a routing decision or a warmup behavior tied to autoscaler activity.
- We’ll scope a provisional credit estimate if the window meets the SLA availability definition, and we’ll start a postmortem within 48 hours.

Can you confirm the sample trace id you sent is: BH-20261117-CHK-7f9c? If you have any additional traces, please forward them.

Jonas
Jonas Weber
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: david.kim@redwood.com
To: jonas.weber@redwood.com, Elena Morales <elena@blueharborpay.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 09:01:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Spike of 503s this morning — preliminary telemetry and window

Elena / team — preliminary findings from a fast pass of telemetry:

- Observed spike start: 2026-11-17T08:05:12-08:00
- Observed spike end: 2026-11-17T08:43:29-08:00
- Error mode: elevated 503s correlated with increased tail latency and a short-lived routing shift to canary nodes in the us-west-2 region.
- Likely cause (initial): a canary warmup + autoscaler transient leading to increased queuing on a subset of shards, followed by temporary routing away from cold nodes.

I’m attaching a short trace summary (trace_summary.txt) and will upload a raw trace bundle to the drive link in ~30 minutes (raw_traces_bundle_20261117.tar.gz).

Prelim position on credit eligibility: based on the tenant-level traffic and the observed error window, this appears to meet the service availability impact threshold for a proportional credit. Final determination requires the raw traces + cross-check with routing policy (canary fallbacks are generally treated as availability-impacting if they result in errors for the tenant).

Action items:
- I will open INF-4732 for the RCA and include the raw trace bundle.
- If BlueHarbor prefers, we can schedule a 30-minute sync at 10:00 PST for a quick readout.

-david
David Kim
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
attachments: trace_summary.txt (text)
From: Elena Morales <elena@blueharborpay.com>
To: david.kim@redwood.com, jonas.weber@redwood.com
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 09:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Spike of 503s this morning — preliminary telemetry and window

Thanks David — that timing matches what we saw.

Confirming the trace id: BH-20261117-CHK-7f9c is one of the failures; I’m attaching a second full trace (forwarded) and a CSV with failed order ids. Please prioritize the raw traces for the 08:05–08:45 window — we need them to validate transaction-level impact.

Two asks: can you both confirm (1) whether the canary fallback will count toward the SLA (you’ve indicated yes provisionally), and (2) share an estimated credit range we should tell finance (ballpark is fine). We’ll join the 10:00 PST readout.

Elena
From: jonas.weber@redwood.com
To: Elena Morales <elena@blueharborpay.com>
Cc: david.kim@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Spike of 503s this morning — provisional credit stance and next steps

Hi Elena — quick update after David’s collection:

- Raw traces and routing logs have been uploaded to the Drive link (see related_links). The raw bundle name is raw_traces_bundle_20261117.tar.gz and the short trace summary is attached (trace_summary.txt).
- Provisional credit stance: given the tenant-level impact and the fact the routing fallback produced end-user errors, this meets the definition for a proportional credit. We’ll calculate the exact amount after the full RCA but expect a prorated credit equivalent to 0.5–1.5% of November invoice as a ballpark (subject to formal adjudication).
- RCA timeline: initial postmortem draft within 48 hours, final RCA and remediation plan within 7 business days.

Next steps for BlueHarbor: please confirm whether you want a formal credit request submitted now (we can start internal approvals to speed the timeline) and whether you’ll attend the 10:00 PST readout.

Thanks for flagging this — we’ll treat INF-4732 as high priority and follow up with the postmortem notes.

Jonas
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
attachments: none
